eq_9_95_resolution.method: rendered PDF page (pdf index 159, printed p.160) region containing Eq.(9.95) at 4x zoom and read visually
eq_9_95_resolution.finding: The source genuinely writes sqrt(1 - |A_ij|), NOT sqrt(1 - |A_ij|^2). This is CORRECT, not a typo: Eq.(9.95) is a SQUARE-ROOT entry oracle whose |0> amplitude is sqrt(A_ij), so the two squared amplitudes are |sqrt(A_ij)|^2 + |sqrt(1-|A_ij|)|^2 = |A_ij| + (1 - |A_ij|) = 1 under the standing assumption ||A||_max <= 1. It is structurally distinct from the amplitude oracle Eq.(9.68)/(9.72), whose |0> amplitude is A_ij itself and therefore requires sqrt(1 - |A_ij|^2). My prior report's characterization of this as a 'source-faithful quirk/typo' was INCORRECT and is withdrawn.
eq_9_95_resolution.impact_on_215: NONE. Item 215 reproduces Eq.(9.95) exactly as the source has it (sqrt(1-|A_ij|)) and it is the mathematically correct normalization for a square-root oracle. The assumption string in 215 ('O_A loads the square root sqrt(A_ij)') correctly flags this as a square-root oracle. 215 remains ACCEPT; the source-vs-semantic label is consistent.

superseding_items.notes: REVISED after skeptical edge-case pass. The core (1,1)-block-encoding identity <0|<i|O_A|0>|j> = A_ii delta_ij is correct and holds for ALL diagonal A with ||A||_max <= 1, including A=0 (both sides 0) - the graded identity portion is fine. However the OPTIMALITY discussion contains an unqualified edge-case overclaim: the reference answer, rubric r4, semantic_steps[4] and native_nl assert that for ||A|| < 1 'a smaller alpha = ||A|| is achievable, e.g. by encoding A/||A||'. This FAILS for the zero matrix A=0, which is in the stated domain (||A||_max = 0 <= 1): (i) 'encoding A/||A||' is division by zero / undefined; (ii) a subnormalization factor must be strictly positive, and the infimum of valid alpha for A=0 is 0 but is UNATTAINED, so there is no 'smaller achievable alpha = ||A|| = 0'. The claim 'alpha = 1 is globally optimal iff ||A|| = 1, otherwise not optimal' is correct only for A != 0; at A=0 alpha=1 is simply one of infinitely many valid (never-optimal, no-minimum) choices. FIX (minimal): add the qualifier ||A|| > 0 (equivalently A != 0) to the 'smaller alpha achievable' statement in reference_answer, rubric r4, semantic_steps[4] and native_nl core_summary; optionally note the A=0 degenerate case where no positive-minimal alpha exists. Pending that qualifier. (This is a narrow, honestly-reported defect; the earlier coordinator-flagged false-global-optimality claim WAS fixed, this is a further corner the fix did not cover.)
